synthesis.gap_summary:
hex_agent is architecturally AHEAD of my_agents on the hard parts: a frozen-lifecycle microkernel with a single tool chokepoint (core/kernel.py execute_tool), middleware pipeline, ToolPort/DelegationPort protocols, SafeToolPort+ToolPolicy gating, RoleSpec/Skill/Lens composition, SQLite-checkpointed dynamic supervisor (Agent-O), and the E21 control-plane CONTRACTS. So the kernel/registry/schemas/roles-loader/orchestration framework are all already_in_hex=full — do NOT port them.

What hex genuinely LACKS, verified by reading source:
1. discipline/json_gate.py _repair (lines 24-50) does ONLY trailing-comma removal + bracket-balancing. It has none of my_agents' repair_rules.py pipeline (python-literal True/False/None, single-quote coercion, unquoted-key fix, control-char escaping, largest-JSON-region extraction). parse_action (line 91-96) only checks for an 'action' field — no candidate ladder, no ast.literal_eval fallback, no structured near-context errors. This is the single highest-value, lowest-risk, purely-offline gap.
2. supervisor/evidence.py classifies evidence by `kind` but does ZERO content-addressing — no sha256, no bytes, no ArtifactRef. my_agents' artifact_protocol.py (ArtifactRef sha256/bytes/producer + compact_metadata briefing) is a clean offline upgrade for the Blackboard.
3. roles/library/lenses/ has only 2 lenses (correctness, requirements). my_agents ships ~40 hand-written LensSpecs across 9 departments — pure YAML-convertible data.
4. toolbox/filesystem.py has only FsRead/FsWrite/FsList — no str_replace/insert/write_lines count-guarded editing primitives.
5. No code_index (AST symbol/reference index) and no lint_test (py_compile/ruff/test) validation tools — both pure-stdlib, offline, and feed finish_gate evidence. Confirmed absent.
6. No app-level ledger with a QUERYABLE surface (append/tail/search/get/stats). observability/event_log is a per-run event STREAM, a different concern.
7. observability/inspect.py only supports --kind; missing --status/--tool/--text filters, summarize_event() human formatter, and metrics columns.
8. No core/runtime_paths.py: `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` is duplicated across core/bootstrap.py, observability/event_log.py, safety/sandbox.py, ui/server.py (confirmed 4 files).
9. control/commands.py is purely typed contracts — no free-text->RuntimeCommand NLU parser, no runtime-invariant denylist. The E21 in-run injection path is unwired.
10. safety/policy.py already has classify_terminal + GIT_MUTATIONS deny + AGENT_ALLOW_GIT_MUTATIONS — so my_agents' "hard tool policy" is ALREADY THERE; only a positive command-allowlist (run-test whitelist) is a real enrichment.

synthesis.tier1_afk:
BUILD-NOW BUNDLE (ranks 1-8): a coherent, fully-offline, architecturally-clean upgrade to hex's output-discipline, evidence, and capability layers. Every item lands behind an existing seam (no bolt-ons), needs zero live LLM/network, and is unit-testable in tests/ + tests_audit/. They are independent enough to ship incrementally but cluster around three themes hex genuinely lacks: (A) robust JSON salvage, (B) content-addressed evidence + richer lenses, (C) read-only code intelligence + validation tools + better editing/inspection.

Rationale & suggested order:
1. core/runtime_paths.py FIRST (rank 4) — it is foundational: ranks 2, 7, 9 want a single var-layout owner, and it removes confirmed 4-file PROJECT_DIR duplication. Smallest blast radius, unblocks the rest. (Build it first even though it ranked 4 on value.)
2. JSON repair-rule pipeline (rank 1) — highest value-to-risk; pure str->str rules straight into discipline/json_gate.py with exhaustive tests_audit/ cases (feed broken JSON, assert repaired). hex's current _repair becomes one entry in the chain.
3. ArtifactProtocol sha256/ArtifactRef + compact_metadata (rank 2) into supervisor/evidence.py + state.py — content-addressing the Blackboard; depends on runtime_paths for the artifact dir.
4. file_editor primitives str_replace/insert/write_lines (rank 5) into toolbox/filesystem.py behind SafeToolPort — independent, temp-dir tests.
5. code_index AST tool (rank 6) — new read-only toolbox capability, pure stdlib ast/re, bounded by max_files.
6. lint_test tool (rank 7) — new validation capability feeding finish_gate; ruff optional/degrades; wire PYTHONPATH via runtime_paths.
7. Lens catalog (rank 3) — ~40 YAML lens files; pure data, validated by LensRegistry.load_dir + lint.
8. inspect.py filter enrichment (rank 8) — --status/--tool/--text + summarize_event + metrics columns; dev-experience polish on the existing event schema.

Each gets matching tests under tests/ (offline unit) and a roundtrip/property test in tests_audit/ for any new persisted contract (ArtifactRef serialization, lens YAML integrity, repaired-JSON properties). Rerun tools/gen_map.py after adding modules. This bundle is genuinely shippable unattended because nothing here touches the live orchestration loop or needs an LLM/network — it is exactly hex's offline-deterministic test culture.

features.name: MCP client/adapter wiring (call_mcp_tool + MCPToolAdapter + feature.install)

areaCatalogs.notes:
How my_agents wires MCP into its capability layer (the key question): the agent only emits JSON tool actions; the JsonGate -> core.capabilities.call_tool -> AgentKernel routes to a single MCPToolAdapter (features/mcp_tools/adapter.py) that implements an execute(ToolRequest)->dict port — structurally identical to hex_agent's ToolPort. The adapter calls features/mcp_tools/client.call_mcp_tool, which is the whole engine: (1) _resolve_tool maps alias/bare/server.tool names to canonical (server, tool, args), (2) validate_tool_args checks the declarative schema in schemas.py, (3) check_tool_policy applies hard deny rules, (4) _call_mcp_tool launches the server over stdio (asyncio.run + stdio_client + ClientSession, one subprocess per call), (5) _dump_result normalizes to a flat {ok, server, tool, ...} dict. feature.install() bulk-registers every MCP_TOOL_NAMES entry + TOOL_ALIASES as kernel capabilities and sets the adapter as a fallback executor. config.py declares 18 servers (15 local python -m + filesystem/git/context7 via npx) with selective env-key passthrough.

Mapping onto hex_agent: this is a clean ONE-PORT bridge. hex_agent already has the harder pieces — ToolPort protocol (core/ports.py), CapabilityRegistry.register_tool with kind/idempotent/risk descriptors, SafeToolPort path-jail/policy chokepoint (safety/), CapabilityResult, and richer RAG. So the MCP transport is 'partial' in hex: the seam exists, only an MCPToolPort adapter + stdio launcher + result normalizer + schema/alias registry need porting. Concretely: add a feature module that, per remote MCP tool, registers an MCPToolPort(name) wrapping call_mcp_tool, behind the existing SafeToolPort, with tool descriptors derived from schemas.py metadata (risk/read_only/changes_file -> hex's kind/idempotent/risk). Two design deltas worth noting: (a) my_agents spawns a fresh stdio subprocess PER CALL (simple, no session reuse) — hex_agent may want a pooled/persistent ClientSession for latency; (b) my_agents duplicates path-jail on both client and server side, whereas hex_agent already jails at SafeToolPort, so the client-side normalization is redundant.

Highest-value, offline, no-equivalent ports (recommend first): code_index (AST index, pure stdlib), lint_test (validation evidence for finish_gate, stdlib+optional ruff), file_editor str_replace/write_lines/insert primitives (count-guarded edits), and the schemas.py declarative per-arg validation + auto tool-prompt generation (fills a real gap in hex's registry). Medium: issue tracker (SQLite work-items for delegation handoffs), ledger (overlaps event_log), terminal risk-classifier (enriches existing Terminal), search/fetch (network-gated). Lower/redundant: rag (hex already richer = full), pdf_text_extraction (duplicate of document), obsidian/document (overlap fs; keep only the secret-scan guard -> control/redaction), docker/playwright (heavy deps, not offline-testable, niche). The hard policy + git-mutation env opt-in is a small pattern that should fold into hex's existing safety/policy ToolPolicy rather than be ported wholesale.

features.name: IntentRouter + RouteDecision schema (deterministic intent classifier)
features.summary: A pure, LLM-free keyword/regex classifier that maps a user request to one of 12 IntentTypes (GENERAL_KNOWLEDGE, CODE/REPO/DEBUG_TASK, PRODUCT_BUILD_TASK, AGENT_CREATION, RESEARCH_REQUIRED, WRITING/PLANNING/NEUROSCIENCE/PHILOSOPHY/MIXED). Emits a frozen RouteDecision dataclass with confidence, needs_repo/code/web/memory flags, target_department, execution_mode (single/sequential/parallel) and an ordered steps[] execution plan. Has bilingual (EN+VI) term tables, file-reference detection, and a MIXED_TASK builder that fans into multiple department steps.
features.hex_fit: New seam in front of supervisor.compose_team / a routing port feeding SessionPlan; could live as core/ or supervisor/router.py producing the team/plan input
features.dependencies: Self-contained: only stdlib (re, dataclasses, enum). No agent or LLM deps.

features.name: GlobalSupervisor (department-dispatch over an execution plan)
features.summary: Top-level deterministic supervisor: classifies via IntentRouter, optionally runs a Safety department gate, then dispatches to knowledge/research/coding/software_factory/planning/writing/agent_factory departments per the RouteDecision.steps execution plan, collects department_outputs/validation_evidence/citations/limits, and hands everything to a FinalSynthesisAgent that owns the single user-facing answer. Coding is delegated (not run) unless run_coding=True. Several departments are placeholders.
features.hex_fit: A higher-level router/dispatch layer above supervisor/loop.py TaskLoop; the 'departments produce outputs, one synthesis agent owns the answer' rule maps onto judge/finish + a final-synthesis step
features.dependencies: Imports FinalSynthesisAgent, knowledge agents, ResearchDepartment, SafetyDepartment, IntentRouter; lazy-imports SoftwareFactory/Company orchestrators. Conceptually portable but pulls several agent modules.

features.name: CompanyOrchestratorV05 (fixed 9-stage department pipeline w/ Code/Test repair loop)
features.summary: Hard-coded sequential chain Research->BusinessAnalyst->Planner->Architect->Code->Test->Review->Ledger->Final. Each department returns a uniform {synthesis, route:{next_agent}} envelope; the orchestrator routes purely on route.next_agent (never infers from prose). Bounded Code<->Test repair cycles (max_cycles), explicit blocked_* statuses at every gate, and a success requires the final stage to return next_agent=done with decision=success. run_real() delegates to the LangGraph runtime instead.
features.hex_fit: Contrast pattern to supervisor's dynamic o_decide: this is a static role pipeline. Maps onto a DelegationPolicy/SessionPlan with a fixed agent order + gate-on-route-envelope; repair loop ~ judge_acceptance retry
features.dependencies: Imports 9 concrete agent runtimes (research/business_analyst/planner/architect/code/test/review/ledger/final) + department_v05 helpers. The orchestrator logic is portable; the agents are not in scope here.

features.name: CodeTestOrchestrator (minimal 2-department repair loop)
features.summary: The smallest orchestrator: bounded Code<->Test cycle (max_cycles). Code routes to test_agent or planner; Test routes to review (pass), code (fail/repair), or planner (blocked). On fail it appends the QA execution evidence to the next task prompt as repair context. Returns explicit terminal statuses (ready_for_review / blocked_needs_planning / blocked_after_code / max_cycles_reached).
features.hex_fit: A degenerate 2-role TaskLoop; the repair-context-injection (feed failure evidence back into next prompt) is the reusable idea, maps to run_round + judge retry feeding evidence into the next briefing
features.dependencies: Imports CodeAgent, TestAgent. Loop is trivially portable; agents out of scope.

features.name: SoftwareFactoryOrchestrator (artifact-first spec pipeline + project doc export)
features.summary: Product-to-code planning pipeline (~21 stages: Vision->BRD->PRD->Epics->AC->validators->Domain->BusinessLogic->Technical->Pattern->ImplementationSpec->CodeHandoff->Docs). Key idea: long analysis is written to versioned artifact files under factory_runs/<run_id>/ while the agent protocol JSON stays tiny and carries only path+sha256 refs (control-channel vs analysis-channel split). Iterates FACTORY_AGENTS, stops on first not-ok, writes a hashed summary artifact, computes a next_recommended_command to hand the implementation_spec to the real coding pipeline, and can export/mirror artifacts (manifest.json + README) into a project's docs/ dir.
features.hex_fit: The artifact-ref-by-path/hash envelope and run-scoped artifact dir map onto hex's observability/event_log + a content-addressed artifact store feeding the Broker's store-slice grounding; the 'JSON too small for analysis -> store by ref' rule is a strong pattern for the supervisor Blackboard
features.dependencies: Imports agents.artifact_protocol (make_run_id, write_json_artifact, ensure_artifact_dir), agents.software_factory_agents (FACTORY_AGENTS, StageResult), core.runtime_paths. The orchestrator shell is portable but depends heavily on the artifact_protocol + ~21 factory agents.

features.name: LangGraph role-graph runtime (real LLM coding pipeline)
features.summary: The production LLM/tool runtime. Builds a LangGraph StateGraph over the 9 PIPELINE roles + a shared 'tool' node, with conditional edges all routing through route_next (END when final_message set, 'tool' for tool calls, else next role; force 'final' when step_count>=max_steps). Carries a rich AgentState. Implements: per-role and per-subtask budgets (ROLE_BUDGETS/SUBTASK_BUDGETS), JSON-gate retries with role-specific repair messages (STRICT_JSON_ROLES), required-file extraction + missing_files tracking, repair-mode detection (last_failure -> patch-only, blocks whole-file rewrites via _should_block_whole_file_repair), forced-test/validation actions, finish gate requiring passing validation + cli_demo evidence, tool-result condensing, repeated-tool-call suppression, and EventLogger telemetry. NOTE: graph.compile() with NO checkpointer (no resume).
features.hex_fit: Direct analog to hex supervisor/graph.py + discipline/. hex already has the LangGraph+SQLite-checkpoint, json_gate, budget, condense, finish_gate, event_log as clean seams — this is the messy monolithic ancestor. Reusable specifics: repair-mode patch-only enforcement, required/missing-file tracking, per-subtask budget keys, forced-validation actions

features.name: Hand-rolled orchestrator loop + live HITL UserDirectiveController
features.summary: Pre-LangGraph single-loop runtime: for step in range(max_steps) -> tool_agent(messages) -> parse JSON action -> run tool -> append observation. Tracks a large metrics dict and enforces parse-error caps, repeated/failed-tool-call caps, finish-gate blockers, observation condensing, and pending-code-validation. Distinctive feature: a UserDirectiveController that polls a control dir / inbox.jsonl (or interactive stdin) for LIVE user directives mid-run, can mark an in-flight agent output 'stale', inject directive prompt blocks, and supports force-final ('stop optional work, answer now'). Emits StateEvents for every directive applied/accepted/rejected.

features.name: AgentState TypedDict (coding-pipeline blackboard) + GlobalAgentState (proposed)
features.summary: The shared state for the LangGraph coding pipeline: a total=False TypedDict with task/messages, routing (next_agent/last_agent/step_count/max_steps), parsed_action, role_outputs, tool fields, and rich repair/validation bookkeeping (required_files, missing_files, last_failure, repair_attempts, files_modified, tests_run, review_result, plus repeated_tool_calls/json_retries/role_visits/subtask_visits counters). Doc 17 additionally proposes a code-optional GlobalAgentState (repo_context/research_context/safety_report optional) for non-code tasks.

areaCatalogs.notes:
Big-picture: my_agents/orchestration shows FIVE orchestration styles layered over the same agents — (1) a deterministic intent router + GlobalSupervisor department-dispatch, (2) fixed sequential department pipelines (Company V05, CodeTest), (3) an artifact-first spec pipeline (SoftwareFactory V07), (4) the real LangGraph role-graph runtime, and (5) the legacy hand-rolled loop. Routing everywhere is by an explicit route.next_agent envelope (never prose). docs/17 is a phased roadmap (phases 1-7 'done' as a deterministic wrapper) for evolving a coding-first system into a department-routed general multi-agent system, with hard safety rules (knowledge/research depts cannot write repo files; file writes require a coding/factory route; external content untrusted).

Compared to hex_agent/supervisor: hex is architecturally AHEAD on the *dynamic* path — its Agent-O TaskLoop (compose_team -> o_decide(LLM) -> run_round -> judge_acceptance) does LLM-driven team composition + per-round orchestration on a dataclass Blackboard, with Broker grounding, delegation policy/registry, SQLite checkpoint+resume, and the E21 event emitter — none of which my_agents has (its LangGraph compile() has NO checkpointer). hex also already owns the clean seams (discipline/json_gate, budget, condense, finish_gate; observability/event_log) that langgraph_orchestrator.py mashes into one 1824-line file.

What hex genuinely LACKS (highest-value ports, in order): (1) the IntentRouter / RouteDecision front-door — hex has no request classifier or execution-plan builder above the TaskLoop; low-complexity, fully offline-testable, self-contained. (2) The SoftwareFactory artifact-channel pattern: store long analysis as content-addressed (path+sha256) artifacts and pass only refs in the protocol envelope — a strong fit for the Broker store-slice + a hex artifact store. (3) The live-HITL UserDirectiveController (force-final / mark-stale / mid-run directive injection) which complements hex's E21 control plane. The fixed department pipelines (Company/CodeTest) are mostly superseded by hex's dynamic orchestrator, but two concrete tactics inside langgraph_orchestrator.py are worth lifting into discipline/: repair-mode 'patch-only, block whole-file rewrite' enforcement, and required/missing-file tracking with per-subtask budget keys. Note offline-testability is excellent across the deterministic layers (router, both pipelines, software-factory shell, global supervisor) precisely because my_agents defaults every department to deterministic lenses with --use-llm opt-in; only langgraph_orchestrator.py truly needs a live LLM.

areaCatalogs.area: Output gate + repair loop (my_agents/output_gate/ vs hex_agent/discipline/)

features.name: Deterministic repair-rule pipeline (light_json_repair)
features.summary: A composable set of string-level repair functions chained by light_json_repair(): strip_bom, strip_markdown_fence, extract_largest_json_region (balanced-bracket scanner picking the largest valid object/array), remove_trailing_commas, replace_python_literals (True/False/None -> JSON, string-aware), quote_unquoted_keys, escape_raw_content_field (re-JSON-encodes a raw content value when followed by known sibling keys), escape_control_chars_in_strings (raw newlines/tabs inside strings), convert_single_quoted_values (Python single-quoted JSON tokens -> double, via ast.literal_eval, string-aware), and balance_trailing_delimiters. Each rule is a pure str->str function operating outside-of-strings using a hand-written escape/in-string state machine.
features.hex_fit: discipline/json_gate.py (the _repair function)
features.dependencies: None — pure stdlib (re, ast, json). Fully self-contained; trivial to port verbatim. hex's _repair only does trailing-comma removal + bracket balancing; it lacks python-literal, unquoted-key, single-quote, control-char, and region-extraction rules.

features.name: Candidate-ladder JSON parsing (build_candidates + try_parse_json)
features.summary: build_candidates() produces an ordered, de-duplicated list of progressively-more-repaired variants [base, fenced, light_repair(no-extract), region, light_repair(region)] and the gate tries each in order. try_parse_json() attempts json.loads then ast.literal_eval fallback, capturing structured decode errors (line/col/pos/near-context). repaired_by_code is tracked so callers know whether the model output was salvaged vs clean.
features.hex_fit: discipline/json_gate.py (parse_json_object / _load_object)

areaCatalogs.notes:
Honest comparison: hex_agent's discipline/json_gate.py is intentionally minimal — fence-strip, one regex-based _repair (trailing commas + bracket balance), a 2-variant load plus a brace-scan fallback, and a single 'action'-field schema check. The repair *budget/re-prompt* lives in graph/nodes.py (record_parse_error + build_retry_message, one retry per turn). So hex covers the BASIC parse-and-reprompt case but has none of my_agents' rule engine.

What is genuinely missing in hex and worth porting (all offline-testable, all stdlib at the rule level):
1. The repair_rules.py rule pipeline — every rule is a pure str->str function with deterministic string-state machines; ideal unit-test fodder (feed broken JSON, assert repaired output). This is the single highest-value, lowest-risk port. hex's _repair would become one entry in this chain.
2. The candidate-ladder + literal_eval fallback + structured near-context decode errors.
3. The deterministic-first repair_loop pattern (history-tracked, agent only as last resort) to replace the ad-hoc single-retry in graph/nodes.py.
4. The alias-normalization rules (action/arg synonym maps) — cheap and high recall on local-model output.

What NOT to port wholesale: the schema/tool-resolve/dry-run stages are tightly coupled to features.mcp_tools.{schemas,policy,config} and hex already has CapabilityRegistry + ToolPort + safety/sandbox + policy that supersede them. Adopt the staged-GateResult *pattern* and the typed error_type vocabulary, but source the schemas from hex's registry, not from the my_agents tool tables. The terminal substring denylist is the weakest piece (substring matching is bypassable) and is redundant against hex's existing sandbox.

Offline-testability summary: the repair rules, candidate ladder, alias normalization, schema/tool-args validation, path/content/terminal safety checks, and the repair loop (with a stub repair_agent) are ALL testable with no network/LLM — they are pure functions over strings/dicts. The ONLY part requiring a live model is the optional repair_agent fallback, which is dependency-injected and trivially stubbable.

areaCatalogs.notes: Honest already_in_hex picture: hex_agent is clearly AHEAD on the read/observability half — its ui/server.py has SSE /api/stream with sha256-diffed snapshots, /api/tree + /api/file browsing, bootstrap, and a typed E21 control plane (RuntimeCommand/CommandAck contracts, command_registry, emitter, permission, redaction, snapshot, checkpoint) that my_agents lacks entirely. my_agents is AHEAD on the write/control half: (1) actual process lifecycle control — start AND stop/terminate of runs (hex_agent can only start, and only in-process on a thread pool, with no cancel), and (2) live user-directive injection into a running run, which hex_agent's control/ specifies as contracts but does not wire end-to-end (no NLU free-text parser, no in-run inbox poll, no stale-output marking, no prompt-block injection). Command vocabulary in hex_agent is registry-driven (YAML/registry), so a ported NLU parser should emit registry kinds rather than the hardcoded marker->op map. Honest comparison: hex_agent is clearly MORE advanced than my_agents in this area. hex's roles/ (RoleSpec + Agent + LensRegistry + AgentRegistry) already does everything BaseAgent/role_config/role_agents do, and does it better: (1) the skill+role allowlist derivation (union explicit_tools + skills' allowed_tools + core_tools, minus skill forbidden, forbidden-wins) lives in one place (roles/spec.py) with a documented cycle-break, whereas my_agents bolts allowlists onto each agent ad hoc; (2) hex enforces separation-of-duties structurally — Agent.__init__ rejects a role that doesn't own validation and names no handoff target, and guard_finish blocks self-certification — my_agents only carries test_ownership as opaque passthrough data; (3) hex splits guard_tool_call/guard_finish as pure functions for the loop, vs my_agents' run()-coupled regex post-guard. So BaseAgent/role_config/role_agents/get_agent are already_in_hex=full and NOT worth porting.

What is genuinely worth harvesting (porting candidates, in priority order):
1. The concrete LENS CATALOG (~40 specs across 9 departments, each with purpose + per-lens tool scopes + output_schema) — hex's roles/library/lenses has only correctness.yaml + requirements.yaml. This is pure data, trivially convertible to hex's lens YAML, and is the single highest-value, lowest-risk port in this area. hex_fit: roles/library/lenses/*.yaml.
2. ArtifactProtocol (artifact_protocol.py) — content-addressed ArtifactRef (sha256/bytes/producer/kind) + StageResult + brief/compact-metadata truncation. hex's supervisor/evidence.py classifies evidence kinds but I saw no content-addressing/hashing of artifacts; the sha256+brief_text compaction is a clean, offline, dependency-light upgrade for supervisor/state.py Blackboard artifacts and observability. hex_fit: supervisor/evidence.py + state.py.
3. The deterministic SafetyDepartment sub-agents (permission/risk/prompt-injection/tool-scope) — all pure, offline, no-LLM. PromptInjectionAgent's substring scan and ToolScopeAgent's per-department capability table map naturally onto safety/policy.py and control/ permission+redaction. Low value individually but cheap and offline-testable.
4. The aggressive JSON-action repair parser in base_agent._parse_json_object — only if hex's discipline/json_gate.py lacks brace-balancing/control-char-escaping/single-quote-coercion salvage (it has json_gate but I did not confirm it does multi-strategy repair). Worth a look as a hardening upgrade.

NOT worth porting: the v0.5 department agents (architect/research/review/planner/BA) are mostly hardcoded deterministic stub dicts — scaffold, not logic; their value is already captured by hex's RoleSpec + lens model. The knowledge/ agents are placeholder keyword-branch stubs and are strictly inferior to hex's existing rag/ (Qdrant + memory) — there is no real knowledge/memory mechanism here to harvest. FinalSynthesisAgent is a reasonable deterministic finish-composer but overlaps hex's discipline/finish_gate + supervisor finish path.

Caveat on offline_testable: I marked code_agent/test_agent false because a meaningful test exercises the executor phase (real file_editor/python/lint tools); their lens phase alone is offline. Everything else in this area is genuinely offline (deterministic dicts or stdlib-only), since the bulk of my_agents' agent logic is hardcoded stubs rather than live LLM calls.

Porting = rewriting each skill body into hex's structured sections and declaring tools.

Net recommendation: code-edit and the loader/openai.yaml format are already fully covered (skip). The 3 read-only/guardrail skills (debug-traceback, project-plan, git-review) and run-test are worth porting as ~30-line library/*.md files — they fill content gaps hex_agent does not yet have (only code_review.md + file_edit.md exist). areaCatalogs.notes: hex_agent has NO domain ledger. The only "ledger" hits in hex_agent are inside the vendored harness/ (unrelated SDLC tooling), not in core_agent app code. observability/event_log.py is a DIFFERENT concern: it is an EventBus-driven, per-run, machine event STREAM (sequence+kind+topic, written to var/agent_runs/<run_id>/events.jsonl, with metrics counters and summary.json/index.jsonl). Port priority: capability_suite > dev_checks > doctor > inspect filter-enrichment > Makefile > bootstrap/Brewfile. Caution: every my_agents script imports its own package tree (agents/orchestration/features/tools.event_reader) and assumes var/ runtime dirs + ORCH_MAX_STEPS + LEDGER/ISSUE_DB env; ports must be rebound to hex_agent's core.bootstrap, observability.event_log.runs_dir, supervisor, and config layout. areaCatalogs.notes:
Honest verdict: hex_agent's core is strictly more advanced than my_agents' across the kernel/registry/schemas/ports themselves — do NOT port those. hex_agent already has: frozen-lifecycle kernel + registry (freeze()), a real middleware pipeline around the single execute_tool chokepoint (my_agents has none), ToolCallContext lineage + allowed_capabilities scope enforcement, ToolDescriptor risk/idempotent/kind retry metadata, deep-copied args, deep-frozen config, typed Delegation ports, and the identical CapabilityResult envelope + NullToolPort + config-driven feature loader. my_agents' kernel/registry/schemas/state/bootstrap/loader are essentially earlier ancestors of hex_agent's.

The ONE genuinely high-value, cleanly-missing idea is runtime_paths.py: hex_agent currently re-derives `PROJECT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` in FOUR files (core/bootstrap.py, observability/event_log.py, safety/sandbox.py, ui/server.py) and re-reads AGENT_WORKSPACE_DIR / AGENT_RUNS_DIR ad hoc, with no single owner of the var/ layout and no ensure_runtime_dirs(). Centralizing this removes duplication and gives one extension point for new runtime dirs (test_runs, qdrant_storage). Recommend porting runtime_paths first.

Second tier (medium): a small core/errors.py taxonomy (hex_agent has only control/errors.py ControlContractError) and re-adding the dropped FeatureDescriptor fields (tests/dependencies/category/removable) + configured_feature_tests() so features carry their own verification + dependency metadata — useful for the harness's test gating.

Everything else (typed semantic ports, null search/memory, JsonlLedger, capabilities.py facade) is low value or already covered: the semantic ports route through hex_agent's generic ToolPort/toolbox/rag; JsonlLedger overlaps observability/event_log; and capabilities.py's get_default_kernel() module-singleton actively conflicts with hex_agent's frozen-kernel + per-session ToolCallContext model — do not port it.

areaCatalogs.notes:
hex_agent currently has NO application-level prompt library and NO case-driven eval harness (confirmed: only harness/ tooling prompts under harness/plugins and harness/install, which are unrelated CLI-skill assets; tests/ has no prompt fixtures, no graded-output gate). So this area is genuinely additive.

Highest-value, lowest-friction ports (all offline): (1) business_prompt_lab/run.py's pure scoring core — parse_json_object + evaluate_output + the weighted checks/banned-phrase/template-echo logic — is a ready-made offline JSON-discipline grader that maps cleanly onto hex discipline/json_gate and could become a tests_audit eval gate; (2) the system_prompt.md tool-agent contract as a golden fixture validating hex's json_gate/finish_gate semantics (hex implements the discipline but has no canonical prompt text capturing it); (3) the cases/*.json + p01-p04 prompt ladder + ba_agent_eval JSONL as deterministic golden inputs.

All paths under /Users/uspro/Desktop/Namson/hex_agent/. The architecture is hexagonal/microkernel: one chokepoint (AgentKernel.execute_tool), config-driven feature install, and Protocol-based ports for every swap point.

== ADD A TOOL ==
A tool is any object with `name: str` + `execute(request: ToolRequest) -> dict` (the ToolPort protocol, core/ports.py:19-26). It is NOT installed directly — it is registered by a *feature*. Registration API on CapabilityRegistry (core/registry.py:67-96):
  - register_tool(name, executor, *, feature_name, kind="tool", idempotent=False, risk="low")
  - register_tools(names, executor, ...) for one executor exposing many capability names.
`kind` ∈ model|read|effect|tool; (idempotent, risk) drive retry/policy middleware (core/registry.py:11-20). Resolution: exact name → optional fallback → NullToolPort (core/registry.py:103-112). Registry freezes before first session (core/registry.py:56-61).

== ADD A FEATURE (the primary plugin seam) ==
A feature is a Python module exposing `install(kernel: AgentKernel) -> None` (features/loader.py:22-25). Convention inside install(): build a FeatureDescriptor, call kernel.registry.register_feature(desc), then register its tools. Canonical patterns:
  - Trivial: features/example_echo.py:9-25 (FeatureDescriptor + register_tools).
  - Sandboxed/gated: toolbox/feature.py:10-36 (wraps each tool in SafeToolPort + ToolPolicy, per-tool risk descriptors).
  - Ports + event-emitting + backend-switchable: rag/feature.py:20-121 (build_service from kernel.config['rag'], tools also publish semantic rag.* events via kernel.events.publish).
Enable a feature by adding an entry under `features:` in config/features.yaml with `enabled: true` and `module: <import.path>` (config/features.yaml:1-13). install_configured_features iterates enabled entries and importlib-imports each module (features/loader.py:10-25). Wired by build_kernel → install_configured_features + _install_middleware (core/bootstrap.py:56-66). Entry points: create_kernel(config_path) / build_kernel(config) (core/bootstrap.py:56-70).

== ADD MIDDLEWARE (cross-cutting hook around every tool call) ==
A middleware is a callable matching ToolMiddleware: __call__(request: ToolRequest, nxt: ToolHandler) -> dict (core/middleware.py:11-15). May act before/after, short-circuit, or rewrite the result envelope. Register via kernel.use(mw); registration order = outer→inner (core/kernel.py:57-61). Built-ins are config-wired in _install_middleware in declared order timing→policy→retry→condense (core/bootstrap.py:28-53) from config['middleware'].{timing,policy,retry,condense}.enabled. NOTE: BudgetGuard is intentionally NOT kernel-wired (per-run counter) and must be added per-run. Pipeline freezes before first session (core/kernel.py:48-55).

== ADD A SKILL ==
A skill is a SKILL.md file: YAML frontmatter (name, description, optional triggers) + body sections 'Allowed (tools)' / 'Forbidden (tools)' / 'Steps' / 'Report' (skills/spec.py:1-11, parse_skill at :98-117). Headings matched by substring, case-insensitive. Skills are role-agnostic (declare tool names only, never reference roles). Load via SkillRegistry.load_file / load_dir (recursive *.md) / load_text (skills/registry.py:28-37). Rendered with progressive disclosure: mode='contract' (desc+Allowed+Forbidden) vs 'full' (+Steps+Report) (skills/registry.py:57-76). union_tools feeds the role allowlist (skills/registry.py:79-89); lint() flags unknown tools (:91-99).

== ADD A ROLE ==
A role is a YAML file parsed into RoleSpec (roles/spec.py:90-120). Required fields: name, role, department, system_prompt; optional: allowed_tools, allowed_skills, route_permissions.may_route_to, test_ownership{owns_validation,must_handoff_to}, lenses (roles/spec.py:19,90-114). Runtime allowlist derivation is the single skill↔role meeting point: union(explicit_tools, core_tools, each skill's allowed_tools) minus skill forbidden_tools — forbidden wins (roles/spec.py:53-63). Load via AgentRegistry.load_file / load_dir (non-recursive *.yaml) (roles/registry.py:38-43). build_agent(name) is shared by single (E05) and multi (E10) paths (roles/registry.py:60-66); role_view/list_roles give the slim RoleView the supervisor consumes (:69-79).

== ADD A LENS ==
A lens is a YAML file → LensSpec (name, purpose, optional allowed/forbidden tools, output_schema) (roles/lenses.py:43-61). Load via LensRegistry.load_file/load_dir(*.yaml) (:74-80); a role declares which lenses render into its prompt via the `lenses:` list.

== ADD A DELEGATION TARGET (sub-agent backend) ==
A delegation target implements DelegationPort: name, can_handle(target)->bool, run(request, child_session, progress_sink)->DelegationResult (core/ports.py:32-45). Register on DelegationRegistry.register(handler); resolve(target) fails loudly on zero or ambiguous matches (delegation/registry.py:15-36). Composition: delegation/bootstrap.py create_delegation_service builds a DelegationManager from registry+SessionFactory+store, gated by config['delegation'].enabled / default_target (config/features.yaml:26-28). Related ports: DelegationStorePort, DelegationServicePort (core/ports.py:48-77).

== ADD AN LLM BACKEND ==
LLM is itself a capability (features/llm_chat.py) flowing through execute_tool; the adapter (llm/adapter.py) is OpenAI-compatible, JSON-mode, lazy client, injectable.

== ADD AN OBSERVABILITY SINK / EVENT CONSUMER ==
Everything funnels through EventBus.publish; kernel emits tool.requested/completed/failed with full session lineage (core/kernel.py:80-168). Subscribe any sink(topic, payload) via bus.subscribe; EventLogger.attach_to_bus is the reference consumer mirroring events→JSONL and mapping topics→metrics (observability/event_log.py:102-134). Add a metric by extending _METRICS (observability/event_log.py:17-30) + a topic branch in the sink.

== ADD A CONTROL-PLANE TRANSPORT/STORAGE (E21, seams defined, adapters pending) ==
control/ports.py defines EventSinkPort.emit(event: RuntimeEvent) (control/ports.py:14-21) as the swap point; v1 in-process BusEventSink, future Kafka/Redis/Postgres adapters drop in with no caller change. Transport / Control-Tower UI / reliability are explicitly NOT yet implemented (README.md:8, MAP.md control/ section).

== OUTPUT-DISCIPLINE SEAM ==
discipline/ holds shared, reusable primitives: json_gate (parse_json_object/parse_action/build_retry_message — field-agnostic JSON repair, discipline/json_gate.py:64-104), budget, condense, finish_gate. Middleware/condense.py and middleware/budget.py wrap these for the tool pipeline.

All under /Users/uspro/Desktop/Namson/hex_agent/. New modules go beside their epic peers; MAP.md (auto-generated by tools/gen_map.py) is the index — rerun it after adding files. Each module starts with a one-line docstring naming its epic.

WHERE NEW MODULES GO BY TYPE:
- New tool/feature → a new module under an existing or new top-level package; expose install(kernel). Trivial/demo features live in features/. Domain features get their own package (toolbox/, rag/ are the precedent: package with feature.py + ports.py + service/adapters). Register the module in config/features.yaml.
- New middleware → middleware/<name>.py, exported from middleware/__init__.py, optionally wired in core/bootstrap.py _install_middleware + a config/features.yaml `middleware:` knob.
- New skill → skills/library/<name>.md (SKILL.md format). Loaded via SkillRegistry.load_dir(skills/library).
- New role → roles/library/<name>.yaml. Loaded via AgentRegistry.load_dir (non-recursive).
- New lens → roles/library/lenses/<name>.yaml (loaded deeper, separate from roles).
- New delegation/agent adapter → adapters/agents/<name>.py.
- New port/protocol → that package's ports.py (core/ports.py for tool/delegation; control/ports.py for control plane; rag/ports.py for RAG). Concrete adapters live in <pkg>/adapters or <pkg>/stores_*.py.

NAMING & CONTRACTS:
- Tools: snake_case capability names (fs_read, rag_search). Executors carry a `.name` attr.
- Roles: targets like `agent:general`; role files require name/role/department/system_prompt.
- Tool result envelope: every tool returns a plain dict with at least `ok: bool`; the kernel wraps it into CapabilityResult (core/schemas.py). A tool must never raise to the kernel (caught at core/kernel.py:113-121).
- Data contracts live in core/schemas.py (TaskEnvelope, ToolRequest, CapabilityResult, FeatureDescriptor, Delegation* types).
